text: {watcher} saw everyone who came to the bar, and remembered who drank alone.
Nothing crossed that bar that {watcher} didn’t notice, including the change.
{watcher} kept half an eye on the glasses and half on the door.
{watcher} knew the regulars by their drinks first and their faces second, and the names hardly came into it.
Whoever came or went, {watcher} would have marked it.
{watcher} watched the room the way anyone behind a bar did, without seeming to.
{watcher} kept the door and knew every face that went through it.
Nobody got past {watcher} without being looked up and down, mostly down.
{watcher} watched the lobby the way the job required, which was closely.
A doorman's whole trade was knowing who belonged, and {watcher} knew, or asked.
{watcher} had a look at everyone who came in, and a memory for most of them.
Whoever passed {watcher}'s door got looked over on the way in, and {watcher} judged them on the way out.
{watcher} sold papers from the corner and watched the block over the top of them.
Nothing passed the newsstand that {watcher} missed, and most of it got an opinion.
{watcher} kept half an eye on the street between customers.
A newsstand was a good post for watching, and {watcher} had years of practice at it.
{watcher} saw the corner from both directions and most of the day besides.
Whoever came by, {watcher} had likely seen them coming.
{watcher} worked behind the counter and saw everyone who came up to it.
Nothing moved through the place that {watcher} didn't notice from behind the counter.
{watcher} kept the counter and kept an eye on who sat at it.
A counterman saw every face twice, coming and going, and {watcher} remembered which ones had tipped.
{watcher} watched the room the way anyone did who stood in the same spot all day.
Whoever came in, {watcher} had a look at them from behind the counter.
{watcher} took the tickets at the door and saw every face that came through it.
Nobody got past {watcher} without a ticket, or without being seen trying.
{watcher} minded the door and watched the line the way the job asked.
A ticket-taker saw the whole house go by, one face at a time, and {watcher} had seen plenty.
{watcher} kept a count of who came in, and a memory of most of them.
Whoever bought a ticket walked past {watcher} to do it.
{watcher} ran the elevator and saw every floor anybody wanted.
Nobody moved through the building without {watcher} carrying them there and forming a view on the way.
{watcher} knew who lived where, and who visited whom, from running the elevator all day.
An elevator man learned a building's business without asking for it, and {watcher} knew most of it and kept it between floors.
{watcher} watched the floors go by and remembered who got off where.
Whoever came or went by the elevator, {watcher} was part of the trip.
{watcher} kept the building and knew who came and went by heart.
Nothing happened on the stairs that {watcher} didn't hear about, usually while it was still happening.
{watcher} watched the door the way any landlady did, without appearing to.
A landlady kept track of tenants' comings and goings as a matter of business, and {watcher} made it a pleasure as well.
{watcher} kept a room near the entrance and made a habit of the hallway.
Whoever used the stairs, {watcher} generally knew about it, and generally knew why.
{watcher} walked the block on a fixed round and knew every doorway on it.
Nothing happened on that stretch that {watcher} didn't pass by sooner or later.
{watcher} kept the beat and kept a memory of who belonged on it.
A beat cop learned a block door by door, and {watcher} knew which doors to knock on and which to walk past.
{watcher} came by on a schedule regular enough to set a clock by.
Whoever was out at the wrong hour, {watcher} was likely to have seen them.
{watcher} worked the stand and saw who came and went at that hour.
Nothing left from there that {watcher} didn't get a look at from the seat.
{watcher} kept the stand, watching the street the way any driver waited on a fare.
A cab driver could tell a hurried fare from a patient one, and {watcher} noticed both kinds.
{watcher} had the stand and the view that came with it.
Whoever hailed a cab there, {watcher} had a look at them first.
{watcher} minded the counter and saw everyone who came in for anything at all.
Nothing much happened in that store that {watcher} didn't ring up or recommend a powder for.
{watcher} kept the register near the door and the door in view.
A druggist's counter saw the whole neighborhood eventually, and {watcher} had seen most of it.
{watcher} watched the aisle out of habit, the way anyone did who had been robbed once.
Whoever came through for a paper or a headache powder, {watcher} rang them up and remembered.
Nobody minded who came and went.
No one was posted to see who came and went.
Nobody kept watch there, and nobody ever had.
There was no one to notice who passed through.
It was the kind of place nobody kept an eye on.
Nobody was paid to notice, so nobody did.
Nobody there was paid to keep track of anybody.
There was nobody on duty, and nobody to ask who had been by.
Nobody kept a list of who came and went, on paper or in their head.
Anybody could have come and gone, and nobody would have known it.
Nobody had the job of noticing who came by, and nobody had applied for it.
No clerk, no doorman, nobody behind a counter: nobody saw who came.
